title: Secretary of State of Kansas

context.text: The seat is open. Jennifer Day defeated Sam Lane 86.7% to 13.3% in the August 4 Democratic primary; Pat Proctor was unopposed for the Republican nomination.
Scott Morgan is the nominee of the United Kansas Party, which describes itself as a new moderate party.
The Kansas News Service guide, the Kansas Reflector's primary-night report and The Green Papers list Proctor (R), Day (D) and Morgan (United Kansas) as the candidates for Secretary of State.

candidates.name: Jennifer Day
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4 Democratic primary over Sam Lane.

priorities.text: Voter education and civic engagement for Kansans of all ages, and working with the Legislature to ensure laws protect voting rights and fair access.
Keep voting systems accurate and free from political influence and disinformation.
Give Kansas businesses the tools to thrive and avoid creating barriers for them.

candidates.researchNotes: Her campaign site was not located; information is from her Ballotpedia survey. Her legislative votes were not reviewed.

candidates.name: Pat Proctor
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the August 4 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Restore confidence in elections by increasing transparency, combating non-citizen voting and ballot harvesting, and cleaning up voter rolls.
Turn the Business Division into an 'entrepreneurship engine' for small business owners.

record.text: Says on his campaign site that as chair of the House Elections Committee he has 'championed and enacted into law strong election safeguards: ensuring only US citizens vote, restoring election day as the deadline for casting ballots, and strengthening paper audits of our elections.'

Sponsors a constitutional amendment on the November ballot that would change the Kansas Constitution's wording from 'every' citizen to 'only' citizens being eligible to vote, and championed a law ending the three-day grace period for mail ballots, which a court has blocked, per the Kansas News Service.

candidates.researchNotes: Priorities and background come from his Ballotpedia survey (blocked, not re-read) and, for the record items, his campaign site and the Kansas News Service guide. Legislature bill pages were not checked.

candidates.name: Scott Morgan
candidates.ballotNote: Nominee of the United Kansas Party.

priorities.text: Act as a 'neutral referee' in running elections, saying the chief election officer should be an appointed administrator.
Protect paper ballots, audits, advance voting including mail-in ballots and the three-day grace period for ballots postmarked before Election Day, while keeping rolls accurate.

candidates.researchNotes: Minimal depth: the party is new and no vote share or polling was found; information is from his Ballotpedia survey only.
